page: Microsoft Azure F64amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured within the Famdsv7 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz, providing 64 physical cores mapped directly to 64 dedicated vCPUs with one thread per core. The memory subsystem contains 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per core. In terms of integrated disk resources, the instance includes 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while accelerator hardware is omitted with zero GPUs installed.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance within the top 10% across CPU, memory throughput, and storage-oriented workloads. Multi-core performance is underscored by a stress-ng multi-core result of 233,420.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 115,907.7. Memory operations achieve 412.42 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 193.26 GB/sec for writes. The instance also features vector and encryption execution support via AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and VAES extensions, registering 141,969.41 in PassMark extended instructions and 97,201.6 in cryptographic testing.

Data handling tests demonstrate high operational capacity, highlighted by 170.17 million Redis SET operations per second, 40,360.96 database operations in PassMark, and 96.65 GB/sec static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference yields 5,641.46 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M parameter models and 64.15 tokens per second generation throughput on 7B models.

From an architectural standpoint, dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores paired with high-capacity local NVMe storage deliver consistent compute density without resource contention. However, lack of discrete GPUs limits intensive deep learning training, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. The configuration is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, multi-threaded compilation, compression pipelines, and distributed analytical engines.
description: Microsoft Azure F64amds_v7 is an enterprise-grade virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated physical cores across 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, accompanied by 512.0 GB of RAM and 7560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V without GPU accelerators, the instance incorporates AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. Standardized testing demonstrates top-decile performance across multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth reaching 412.42 GB/sec, and high-frequency key-value storage tasks yielding 170.17 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers dense compute and memory ratios alongside substantial onboard disk capacity, making it technically suited for high-throughput in-memory data stores, distributed database clusters, multi-threaded batch compression, and medium-scale CPU inference workloads.
